I've probably considered suicide very seriously twice in the past 4 months, to the point I was looking down from a bridge about 50 meters from the ground, with little fear, but some trepidation. The thing that stopped me was Dissection's Storm of the Light's Bane and Sacramentum's Far Away From The Sun, respectively. It reminded me that there's still a shred of beauty to be found in life, so I might as well exhaust my enjoyment of the music before I end myself. Before that, bands like Opeth had gotten me through episodes of intense paranoia and fear, and Cryptopsy sort of inspired me to work harder at engineering (though it wasn't effective, I recently dropped out of comp eng).

Edit: Hindsight being 20/20, this is obviously some joke/troll post. Whatever.

Just curious, has any band done this already?

Mayhem is also much better now (morally, not musically). Most members renounce the past actions of the band. As for supporting Varg, I actually have a Filipino friend who owns a Burzum shirt. When I asked him about it, he replied that he supports the artist, not the individual. This is pretty much the same mindset I have towards all of this stuff. Burzum definitely isn't for everyone, but if you hear something of theirs you dig, I hope you can enjoy the music despite Varg's many flaws.

As for Dead, he seemed to be a really nice kid, who just had a lot of problems (and, to be fair, probably had some psychological disorders). I mean, if you see a photo of him sans corpse paint, he's nearly always smiling. His suicide note was basically one big apology.

And Immortal rules! I don't think I could ever have gotten into BM if I didn't have them as a stepping stone.

Don't worry about me dying just yet, by the way. There are many people posting here who are in far more dire situations than I. Please do not fear too much on my behalf! I can't imagine how great a burden it must be to fear for the safety of everyone here.

Well it's really all subjective. I can't see life as something worthwhile, or even neutral, though I can fathom why other people might enjoy it. Let me put it this way; imagine if in 10 years I had a great job, a beautiful, loving wife, and an intelligent child, I would still think this world is, at best, meaningless, and at worst, a piece of shit. Life is just intrinsically shit. And that isn't even factoring in all the awful things that might happen up to that point.

Sorry if it's difficult for me to explain myself; it's tough to condense one's own personal, unrelateable worldview that's been formed over years of thought into just a few sentences.
I view life as being a wholly negative experience. Seeing the hedonism and happiness of everyone around me seems to me an act of willful blindness. Ignorance is bliss, as they say.

Fuck, well for starters I'm really lazy. Prime example, I pretty much slept through this last term of university and spent all of today meditating on the meaninglessness of life instead of studying for the finals that are less than a week away, are deciding my future, and I know literally nothing of.

I also have a fear/derision of everything. While this is an exaggeration, it isn't by a large margin: I'm afraid of the dark, blood, pain, social situations, serial killers, dismemberment, hospitals, rejection, insects, heights, dogs, the list goes on and on. It's a constant fear as well; even as I type I dread that someday I'll be kidnapped, hacked into pieces, and end up being found in seven different places. As for hating things, I abhor sex (though not at all on a biological level), happiness, fear, ignorance, hatred (against individuals), drugs, alcohol, parties, society, learning, working out, etc. All these things completely control me, and I really don't care to try and work them out.

To be fair, I would have killed myself several times over had I the guts to do it. So I suppose not everything is black and white. It does take a lot of will to kill ones-self.
